description:
About the Position

Uppsala University invites applications for a PhD student position on the recycling of solid electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries. The project focuses on lithium halide solid electrolytes, a promising class of materials for next-generation solid-state cells, and develops closed-loop recycling routes that recover and regenerate these materials after cell use. The doctoral student will connect materials synthesis, electrochemical characterisation and recycling process development, contributing to a sustainable European battery value chain in which critical raw materials stay in circulation.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral employment under the Swedish collective agreement, based in the university's battery and electrochemistry research environment. The doctoral student will fabricate and test solid-state cells, characterise recycled electrolyte materials against freshly synthesised references, and evaluate how recycling affects performance, purity and process economics. The work combines laboratory research with data analysis and collaboration with project partners across academia and industry.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree (or equivalent) in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or a closely related field, with a strong interest in electrochemistry and battery materials. Experience with synthesis, electrochemical testing or recycling processes is an advantage, as is an affinity for circular-economy questions. Applications are submitted through Uppsala University's Varbi recruitment system with a CV, transcripts, references and a statement of research interests, and admission is judged on academic record, research potential and fit with the project.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD employment in battery materials research
  • Lithium halide solid electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries
  • Closed-loop recycling of critical battery materials
  • Synthesis, cell testing and electrochemical characterisation
  • Circular battery value-chain research at Uppsala University
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system
